> **Pipeline step 03 — fork-length diagnostics (supporting).**
>
> **Purpose.** Shows that the persistent S-shaped DHARMa QQ of the fork-length models is
> bimodality in fork length (hatchery vs natural size composition), locates the grouping
> variable, and compares split / mixture alternatives. The reported model keeps origin OUT of the
> model set and lumped; this notebook documents why.
>
> **Inputs.** `data/tps_forklength_data.csv`, `fits_tps_fl_kfold/fit_tps_fl_9.rds`.
> **Outputs.** density figures, comparison fits and `fit9_fixef_comparison.csv` under
> `fits_tps_fl_kfold/`.

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
`fit9_family_comparison.Rmd` swapped fit 9 across gaussian, lognormal (log link,
multiplicative variance), Gamma (log link, variance ∝ mean²), skew_normal (asymmetry), and a
distributional `sigma ~ .` variant — additive/multiplicative, symmetric/skewed, and mean-dependent
variance. **Every one keeps the same S-shaped DHARMa QQ plot.** When the misfit is invariant to that
much variation in the *conditional distribution*, the conditional distribution is almost certainly
not the problem. (The `sigma` variant only "passed" residual-vs-predicted by widening the quantile
envelope, not by removing curvature — a statistic passing for the wrong reason. It's set aside.)

A persistent S-shaped QQ is the classic signature of **bimodal (multimodal) scaled residuals**: the
empirical CDF rises slowly through the first mode, quickly across the gap, then slowly through the
second, drawing out an S against the uniform expectation. Every family tried is unimodal, so none can
reproduce a two-humped conditional distribution — which is why they fail *identically*, and it's
consistent with dispersion passing (two modes can have the right overall SD but the wrong shape).
Year classes are already ruled out. This notebook attacks the bimodality directly:

1. Plot raw `ForkLength` density, confirm two modes and locate the gap.
2. Facet/colour that density by every categorical variable in the data.
3. Test residuals against each candidate factor with `plotResiduals(sim9, form = factor)`, plus a
   station-grouped `recalculateResiduals()` view (observation-level vs station-level misfit).
4. Two pieces of due diligence: measurement **heaping** and unmodelled **mean-structure curvature**.
5. If a measured covariate cleaves the modes → add it, refit, S-curve should collapse. If nothing
   measured explains it → fit a principled **two-component gaussian mixture** (`brms` native).

> Note on the `tps` prefix: it denotes the *Tidal Parr Study*, **not** a thin-plate spline. Fit 9 is
> linear in the z-scored predictors — no `s()` smooth is present — so step 4's curvature check is a
> genuine, separate hypothesis rather than a re-check of something already in the model.

> **Findings from the rendered run (2026-07-01).** `ForkLength` is clearly two-humped (modes ≈43 and
> ≈85 mm, gap ≈68). **`ChinookClipped` origin is the grouping variable**: `Natural` fish sit on the
> lower hump, `Clipped (hatchery)` on the upper, and origin is the *only* candidate flagged by **both**
> the DHARMa Levene (unequal variance) and within-group-uniformity tests. `shoreline_Class` trips only
> the uniformity flag; `Gear` and all others are n.s. Curvature check: the residual-vs-predictor
> *medians are flat* → no missing smooth; the quantile-test flags are the two-mode spread leaking in.
> Heaping: none (`ForkLength %% 5` ≈ uniform). Station-grouping makes the KS *worse* (D 0.15→0.25) → the
> split is observation-level, not among-station. Refits: base gaussian KS D=0.150 (p=0.005); **+Origin**
> D=0.138 (p=0.013); **+Origin & sigma~Origin** D=0.140 (p=0.011, dispersion now perfect, and natural
> fish confirmed ~1.9× wider: `sigma_OriginNatural`=+0.62 [0.11,1.07] on log scale). So a single binary
> covariate *reduces but does not clear* the flag — the `Natural` group itself spans both modes and
> origin is partly confounded with the existing predictors, so the fully principled resolution is the
> **two-component mixture** (step 5b). Crucially, the ecological fixed effects (distance / depth / out30
> / water_year_day) are **stable** across all variants — `out30_z` stays ≈ −12.5, every coefficient
> within its CI — so the KS flag does not threaten the inferential target (step 5c).

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(DHARMa)
library(patchwork)
library(kableExtra)

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```

Config — reuse the family-comparison output area so all of fit 9's exploratory work lives together.
```{r config}
FIT_DIR      <- "fits_tps_fl_kfold"                     # where fit_tps_fl_9.rds already lives
OUT_DIR      <- file.path(FIT_DIR, "fit9_bimodality")   # diagnostics + mixture fit go here
if (!dir.exists(OUT_DIR)) dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE)

n_sim_dharma <- 1000   # same as DHARMa_testing.Rmd / the family-comparison notebook
```


## Data

Loaded and typed identically to the kfold notebook, then `ChinookClipped` is cleaned into a tidy
2-level **origin** factor (raw values are a mix of `no/No/yes/Yes` plus one `NA`). No modelled
variable is touched, so row alignment with the fitted model is preserved.
```{r data}
d_fl <- read_csv("data/tps_forklength_data.csv")
d_fl$Edge_Type   <- factor(d_fl$Edge_Type)
d_fl$StationCode <- factor(d_fl$StationCode)

# Origin: hatchery-clipped vs natural. Case-fold, map to two clean levels, keep NA as NA.
d_fl <- d_fl |>
  mutate(
    Origin = case_when(
      str_to_lower(ChinookClipped) == "yes" ~ "Clipped (hatchery)",
      str_to_lower(ChinookClipped) == "no"  ~ "Natural",
      TRUE                                  ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Origin = factor(Origin),
    Month  = factor(Month)   # treat as categorical for the split check
  )
```

Reconstruct the exact rows fit 9 used (drop NA in the response + modelled predictors), so every
candidate factor lines up 1:1 with the DHARMa residual vector. The `stopifnot` is the guardrail — if
`brm()` dropped a row we didn't, the whole faceted/`form=` analysis would be silently misaligned.
```{r model-rows}
fit9_gaussian <- readRDS(file.path(FIT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9.rds"))

model_vars <- c("ForkLength", "distance_along_channel_z", "distance_m_z",
                "start_depth_z", "out30_z", "water_year_day_z", "StationCode")

d_model <- d_fl |> tidyr::drop_na(all_of(model_vars))

stopifnot(nrow(d_model) == nrow(fit9_gaussian$data))
message("Modelled rows: ", nrow(d_model), " (matches fit_tps_fl_9$data)")
```

Candidate grouping variables — the categoricals that could split fork length into two clusters for a
non-age reason. `Tide` (100/134 NA) and `Target_Caught` (constant) are excluded as unusable.
```{r candidates}
candidate_factors <- c(
  "Origin",              # hatchery-clipped vs natural — top non-age suspect (size dimorphism)
  "Gear",                # capture method: 4 gears with different size selectivity
  "Habitat2020",         # habitat split
  "Region2020",          # spatial split
  "Edge_Type",           # shoreline edge class (already used by some fits, not fit 9)
  "shoreline_Class",     # shoreline class
  "Sac_Water_Year_Type", # water-year type
  "Month"                # seasonal / growth-stage split
)

# Cell counts, so tiny-cell factors (e.g. Region2020 has a single Napa row) are read with care.
purrr::walk(candidate_factors, function(v) {
  cat("\n== ", v, " ==\n", sep = "")
  print(table(d_model[[v]], useNA = "ifany"))
})
```


## Step 1 — raw ForkLength density: confirm the two modes and the gap

```{r raw-density, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
gap_guess <- NA_real_   # set after eyeballing, e.g. gap_guess <- 70; used only for the reference line

p_raw <- ggplot(d_model, aes(ForkLength)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), binwidth = 3,
                 fill = "grey80", colour = "white") +
  geom_density(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.5) +
  { if (!is.na(gap_guess)) geom_vline(xintercept = gap_guess, linetype = 2, colour = "red") } +
  labs(title = "Raw ForkLength — is it two-humped?",
       x = "Fork length (mm)", y = "density") +
  theme_minimal()

p_raw
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit9_forklength_density_raw.png"), p_raw,
       width = 8, height = 4, dpi = 200)
```


## Step 2 — density split by each candidate factor

The same density, coloured/faceted by each candidate. Whichever variable cleaves the two modes
*cleanly* (one hump per level, minimal overlap) is the answer.
```{r density-by-factor, fig.width=11, fig.height=13, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
density_by <- function(v) {
  dat <- d_model |> filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]))
  ggplot(dat, aes(ForkLength, fill = .data[[v]], colour = .data[[v]])) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_rug(aes(colour = .data[[v]]), alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    labs(title = v, x = "Fork length (mm)", y = "density",
         fill = NULL, colour = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
}

density_grid <- wrap_plots(map(candidate_factors, density_by), ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(title = "ForkLength density split by candidate grouping variable")
density_grid
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit9_forklength_density_by_factor.png"), density_grid,
       width = 11, height = 13, dpi = 200)

# Faceted (small-multiple) view — sometimes reads more cleanly than overlaid densities.
faceted_by <- function(v) {
  dat <- d_model |> filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]))
  ggplot(dat, aes(ForkLength)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 4, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[v]]), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(title = v, x = "Fork length (mm)", y = "count") +
    theme_minimal()
}
```


## Step 3 — DHARMa residuals vs each candidate factor

`plotResiduals(sim9, form = factor)` bins the scaled residuals by factor level and runs a
within-level KS + a Levene homogeneity test: if a factor is driving the misfit, its levels sit at
systematically different residual locations. Built once here; the gaussian fit is already on disk so
this is fast.
```{r sim9}
set.seed(123)
sim9 <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = fit9_gaussian, n = n_sim_dharma, plot = FALSE)
stopifnot(length(sim9$scaledResiduals) == nrow(d_model))
```

```{r resid-vs-factor, fig.width=10, fig.height=14, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
png(file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit9_resid_vs_candidate_factors.png"),
    width = 1900, height = 2600, res = 200)
par(mfrow = c(ceiling(length(candidate_factors) / 2), 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (v in candidate_factors) {
  # DHARMa drops points with NA in `form`; recode to a visible level so nothing is silently omitted.
  f <- addNA(factor(d_model[[v]]), ifany = TRUE)
  plotResiduals(sim9, form = f, main = v, xlab = v)
}
mtext("fit 9 — DHARMa residuals vs candidate grouping variables", outer = TRUE, cex = 1.2)
dev.off()

par(mfrow = c(ceiling(length(candidate_factors) / 2), 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (v in candidate_factors) {
  f <- addNA(factor(d_model[[v]]), ifany = TRUE)
  plotResiduals(sim9, form = f, main = v, xlab = v)
}
mtext("fit 9 — DHARMa residuals vs candidate grouping variables", outer = TRUE, cex = 1.2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Station-grouped residuals — is the misfit observation-level or station-level? If aggregating to
station makes the QQ straighten, the two modes live *between* stations (a spatial/among-station
split a single random intercept isn't absorbing); if it persists, they live *within* station.
```{r resid-grouped-station, fig.width=8, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
sim9_station <- recalculateResiduals(sim9, group = d_model$StationCode)

png(file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit9_resid_grouped_by_station.png"),
    width = 1600, height = 1600, res = 200)
plot(sim9_station)
dev.off()

plot(sim9_station)
```


## Step 4 — due diligence: heaping and mean-structure curvature

**Heaping.** If fork length is recorded to the nearest 5/10 mm the response is effectively
discretized and no continuous family will ever pass the KS test, independent of bimodality. Quick
check: the modulo tables and a fine-binned histogram should *not* show a comb.
```{r heaping, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
cat("ForkLength %% 5:\n"); print(table(d_model$ForkLength %% 5))
cat("\nForkLength %% 10:\n"); print(table(d_model$ForkLength %% 10))

ggplot(d_model, aes(ForkLength)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "grey30") +
  labs(title = "Fine-binned ForkLength (1 mm) — comb-like spikes would indicate heaping",
       x = "Fork length (mm)", y = "count") +
  theme_minimal()
# In this dataset the modulo counts are near-uniform -> no heaping; documented, not a defect.
```

**Mean-structure curvature.** Fit 9 is linear in each z-scored predictor. If a residual-vs-predictor
plot bows systematically, a real smooth (`s()`) may be missing — a misspecification that can co-occur
with bimodality. `plotResiduals` overlays quantile-regression lines and flags significant deviation.
```{r resid-vs-continuous, fig.width=10, fig.height=7, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
cont_preds <- c("distance_along_channel_z", "distance_m_z", "start_depth_z",
                "out30_z", "water_year_day_z")

png(file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit9_resid_vs_continuous_preds.png"),
    width = 1900, height = 1300, res = 200)
par(mfrow = c(2, 3), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (v in cont_preds) plotResiduals(sim9, form = d_model[[v]], main = v, xlab = v)
mtext("fit 9 — DHARMa residuals vs continuous predictors (curvature check)", outer = TRUE, cex = 1.1)
dev.off()

par(mfrow = c(2, 3), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (v in cont_preds) plotResiduals(sim9, form = d_model[[v]], main = v, xlab = v)
mtext("fit 9 — DHARMa residuals vs continuous predictors (curvature check)", outer = TRUE, cex = 1.1)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```


## Step 5a — if a measured covariate explains the split: add it and refit

If step 2/3 point at one factor (say `Origin`), add it to fit 9's mean structure and re-run the
DHARMa panel. If bimodality was the mechanism, the S-curve should collapse. Interactive only — this
is a real 4-chain refit. **Edit `SPLIT_VAR` to whichever variable the diagnostics implicate.**
```{r refit-with-covariate, eval=FALSE}
SPLIT_VAR <- "Origin"   # <- set from step 2/3 findings (e.g. "Origin", "Gear", "Habitat2020")

d_split <- d_fl |> tidyr::drop_na(all_of(c(model_vars, SPLIT_VAR)))

fit9_form_base <- ForkLength ~ distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z + start_depth_z +
                               out30_z + water_year_day_z + (1 | StationCode)
fit9_form_split <- update.formula(fit9_form_base, paste(". ~ . +", SPLIT_VAR))

fit9_split_path <- file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("fit_tps_fl_9_plus_", SPLIT_VAR, ".rds"))
if (file.exists(fit9_split_path)) {
  fit9_split <- readRDS(fit9_split_path)
} else {
  fit9_split <- brm(
    formula   = fit9_form_split,
    family    = gaussian(),
    data      = d_split,
    prior     = c(set_prior("normal(0,5)", class = "b")),
    iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, chains = 4,
    control   = list(max_treedepth = 10, adapt_delta = 0.95),
    save_pars = save_pars(all = FALSE)
  )
  saveRDS(fit9_split, fit9_split_path)
}

set.seed(123)
sim9_split <- simulateResiduals(fit9_split, n = n_sim_dharma, plot = FALSE)

png(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("fit_tps_fl_9_plus_", SPLIT_VAR, "_2x2.png")),
    width = 1800, height = 1400, res = 200)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
plotQQunif(sim9_split); plotResiduals(sim9_split)
testDispersion(sim9_split); testZeroInflation(sim9_split)
mtext(paste0("fit 9 + ", SPLIT_VAR), outer = TRUE, cex = 1.2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1)); dev.off()

pp_check(fit9_split, ndraws = 100) + ggtitle(paste0("fit 9 + ", SPLIT_VAR))
```

If the split factor also failed the **Levene** (unequal-variance) test — as `Origin` does here — an
additive intercept can't straighten the QQ on its own. Let `sigma` depend on it too (a "simple"
gaussian DHARMa still supports). In the rendered run this fixed the dispersion perfectly and confirmed
`Natural` fish are ~1.9× wider, but the KS flag only eased to D≈0.14 (p≈0.011) — because the `Natural`
group itself spans both modes. That residual is what the mixture in 5b is for.
```{r refit-sigma-by-split, eval=FALSE}
d_split <- d_fl |> tidyr::drop_na(all_of(c(model_vars, SPLIT_VAR)))
sigma_form <- bf(
  reformulate(c("distance_along_channel_z", "distance_m_z", "start_depth_z", "out30_z",
                "water_year_day_z", SPLIT_VAR, "(1 | StationCode)"), response = "ForkLength"),
  as.formula(paste("sigma ~", SPLIT_VAR))
)
fit9_sig_split <- brm(
  sigma_form, family = gaussian(), data = d_split,
  prior = c(set_prior("normal(0,5)", class = "b")),
  iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, chains = 4,
  control = list(max_treedepth = 10, adapt_delta = 0.95),
  save_pars = save_pars(all = FALSE)
)
saveRDS(fit9_sig_split, file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("fit_tps_fl_9_", SPLIT_VAR, "_sigma", SPLIT_VAR, ".rds")))

set.seed(123)
sim9_sig <- simulateResiduals(fit9_sig_split, n = n_sim_dharma, plot = FALSE)
png(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("fit_tps_fl_9_", SPLIT_VAR, "_sigma", SPLIT_VAR, "_2x2.png")),
    width = 1800, height = 1400, res = 200)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
plotQQunif(sim9_sig); plotResiduals(sim9_sig)
testDispersion(sim9_sig); testZeroInflation(sim9_sig)
mtext(paste0("fit 9 + ", SPLIT_VAR, ", sigma ~ ", SPLIT_VAR), outer = TRUE, cex = 1.2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1)); dev.off()
```


## Step 5b — if nothing measured explains it: two-component gaussian mixture

The principled model for two subpopulations you can't label. `mixture(gaussian, gaussian)` with
`order = TRUE` constrains the component intercepts (mu1 < mu2) to defeat label switching; the two
`Intercept` priors are seeded near the visual modes from step 1 so the sampler separates the
components cleanly. The `(1 | StationCode)` random intercept and the fixed effects are shared across
both components (one predictor formula → both means), matching fit 9's mean structure. Interactive
only — mixtures are fiddlier and slower than the family swaps.
```{r mixture, eval=FALSE}
# Seed the two component intercepts near the modes you read off the step-1 density.
# EDIT these two numbers to the low/high humps you actually see.
mode_lo <- 45
mode_hi <- 95

mix_form <- bf(
  ForkLength ~ distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z + start_depth_z +
               out30_z + water_year_day_z + (1 | StationCode)
)

mix_priors <- c(
  set_prior("normal(0,5)", class = "b"),                                  # shared slopes
  set_prior(sprintf("normal(%g,20)", mode_lo), class = "Intercept", dpar = "mu1"),
  set_prior(sprintf("normal(%g,20)", mode_hi), class = "Intercept", dpar = "mu2"),
  set_prior("dirichlet(2, 2)", class = "theta")                          # mixing proportion
)

mix_path <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9_mixture2.rds")
if (file.exists(mix_path)) {
  fit9_mix <- readRDS(mix_path)
} else {
  fit9_mix <- brm(
    formula   = mix_form,
    family    = mixture(gaussian, gaussian, order = TRUE),
    data      = d_model,
    prior     = mix_priors,
    init      = 0,                       # 0-init + ordered intercepts avoids label switching
    iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, chains = 4,
    control   = list(max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99),
    save_pars = save_pars(all = FALSE)
  )
  saveRDS(fit9_mix, mix_path)
}

# DHARMa panel + pp_check: if bimodality was the issue, QQ straightens and pp_check recovers 2 humps.
# NOTE: DHARMa >= 0.5 supports only "simple" brms models and may refuse a mixture family. If
# simulateResiduals() errors, build the DHARMa object by hand from brms posterior_predict draws.
set.seed(123)
sim9_mix <- tryCatch(
  simulateResiduals(fit9_mix, n = n_sim_dharma, plot = FALSE),
  error = function(e) {
    message("simulateResiduals() rejected the mixture (", conditionMessage(e),
            ") — falling back to createDHARMa + posterior_predict.")
    yrep <- brms::posterior_predict(fit9_mix, ndraws = n_sim_dharma)   # draws x obs
    createDHARMa(
      simulatedResponse = t(yrep),                                     # obs x draws
      observedResponse  = fit9_mix$data$ForkLength,
      fittedPredictedResponse = apply(yrep, 2, median),
      integerResponse   = FALSE
    )
  }
)

png(file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9_mixture2_2x2.png"),
    width = 1800, height = 1400, res = 200)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
plotQQunif(sim9_mix); plotResiduals(sim9_mix)
testDispersion(sim9_mix); testZeroInflation(sim9_mix)
mtext("fit 9 — two-component gaussian mixture", outer = TRUE, cex = 1.2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1)); dev.off()

pp_check(fit9_mix, ndraws = 100) + ggtitle("fit 9 — 2-component gaussian mixture")
```


## Step 5c — do the ecological conclusions actually move?

The pragmatic test. If the deliverable is the fixed-effect relationships (distance / depth / out30 /
water_year_day → fork length) rather than calibrated predictive intervals, compare those coefficients
between the gaussian fit and whichever alternative fixed the QQ. If they're stable, the defensible
path is to adopt the better model, confirm the estimates hold, and *document* the bimodality as a
feature of the data — a modest KS flag needn't be disqualifying for an honestly-stated inferential
target.
```{r compare-fixef, eval=FALSE}
fixef_tbl <- function(fit, label) {
  as.data.frame(fixef(fit)) |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
    transmute(term, model = label,
              est = Estimate, lwr = Q2.5, upr = Q97.5)
}

# Bind whichever alternatives you actually fit above.
compare_fixef <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fixef_tbl(fit9_gaussian, "gaussian"),
  if (exists("fit9_split")) fixef_tbl(fit9_split, paste0("+", SPLIT_VAR)),
  if (exists("fit9_mix"))   fixef_tbl(fit9_mix,   "mixture2")
)

ggplot(compare_fixef, aes(est, term, colour = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "fit 9 fixed effects — gaussian vs. alternatives",
       subtitle = "if these don't move, the bimodality is a documentable data feature, not a threat",
       x = "estimate (95% CrI)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

write_csv(compare_fixef, file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit9_fixef_comparison.csv"))
```
